_comment: Pattern: bls-signature (e(sig, g2) == e(hm, pk)). Three independent points: sig is the secret BLS signature (G1, 96 hex chars), hm is the public 'message point' (G1, the hash-to-curve output, 96 hex chars), and pk is the public BLS key (G2, 192 hex chars). All three are supplied raw because the circuit only checks the bilinearity equation — it doesn't know sk or m.
_warning: These hex bytes are PLACEHOLDERS. To produce a self-consistent triple, write a small Go script that picks sk and msg, computes pk=[sk]g2, hm=[msg]g1, sig=[sk*msg]g1, then prints the .Bytes() of each. Or just use --test which builds a valid triple internally.
